column1: # contention-sensors.tsv — the REGISTRY of product findings that only show under contention / on a
# freshly grown cluster, and which drill units still sample them (simcluster-speed plan §5.5 X26;
# the accel plan's C1 policy, which promised this file in its acceptance #6 and never wrote it).
# WHY. Every load-discovered defect this suite has produced came from UNENGINEERED contention: #67 under
# 7-way saturation, #66 at -j3, 52's rc=77 at -j6, #70 whenever five grows start together. Every speed
# lever reduces contention (lanes cap concurrent grows; arms run on fresh clusters instead of after their
# siblings; templates skip the grow entirely), so each of those sensors can go dark WITHOUT any drill
# turning red. This file makes that visible: a drill arm that stops sampling a sensor must say so in
# its `# forgoes:` (tests/arm-manifest-lint.sh), the sensor must exist here, and every sensor must still
# have at least one unit that samples it in some regime — or the row says `none-after-split` out loud.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated; tests/contention-registry-check.sh validates):
#   sensor    id, [A-Za-z0-9-]+ (a gotcha number is written without its `#`, which is this file's comment
#             marker), unique; the first word of a drill's `# forgoes:` value must be one of these
#   regime    default | live-grow | none-after-split | H-dependent
#               default          sampled by the ordinary -j sweep as it runs today
#               live-grow        sampled only when grows run uncapped (`run-drills.sh --live-grow`, by hand before a release / after a grow-path change — nothing schedules it)
#               none-after-split no unit samples it any more — recorded, never silently dropped
#               H-dependent      its trigger window moved with the client-liveness constants (plan §5.4)
#   units     space-separated unit names (drill, or drill.arm once the drill has a manifest) that sample it
#   evidence  what the sensor looks like when it fires (a signature, a README anchor, a gotcha id)
